::: {.callout-note title="What this document is"}
A standalone walkthrough of the key files behind our phage–host analysis: what each is, what it shows, and how they chain together. Figures and table snippets are embedded and numbered. Source files: `code/output/0703_phage_host_matrix/`.
:::

# What we are doing

We are a phage-therapy project working with several **sequenced *Pseudomonas* isolates**
(`9-6-2`, `9-2-1`, `10-10-2`, `8-5-2`, `8-10-2`). The goal is to determine **which surface
receptor our phages target** on these bacteria. Our own lytic phages are isolated (plaques) but
**not yet sequenced**, so we cannot read their receptor-binding proteins (RBPs) directly.

We therefore bridge indirectly:

1. **Catalogue** each isolate's surface receptors (@sec-catalogue).
2. Ask which known *Pseudomonas* phages (from the **PharBP** database) infect strains that
   **share those receptors** (@sec-hosts, @sec-presence) — a clue for which phages / RBP classes
   could target our isolates.
3. **Attempt structural folding** (RBP × receptor) to sharpen the clue (@sec-fold) — which proved
   non-informative and is reported as a controlled negative result (@sec-control).

# Part A — Our receptors and who shares them {#sec-partA}

*The primary, clue-level evidence. Does not depend on the folding step in Part B.*

## Our receptor catalogue {#sec-catalogue}

`receptor_by_strain.tsv` organizes all isolates' receptors into **144 unique receptor groups**,
marking overlap across isolates. Groups present in **all 5 isolates (core) = 43**; groups present
**only in 8-10-2 = 46** — a candidate driver of a difference in host range (@tbl-receptor).

| cluster_rep | category | n_strains | product |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| BPBBIK_01263 | FadL | 5 (core) | Long-chain fatty acid transporter |
| BPBBIK_00419 | LptD | 5 (core) | LPS-assembly protein LptD |
| BPBBIK_01078 | OmpA | 5 (core) | OmpA-like domain-containing protein |
| NEEDOG_02224 | FadL | 1 (8-10-2 only) | Long-chain fatty acid transport protein |

: Receptor catalogue (snippet; 144 groups total, 43 core / 46 unique to 8-10-2). {#tbl-receptor}

## The PharBP host list {#sec-hosts}

`pharbp_pseudomonas_hosts.tsv`: from **6,376 *Pseudomonas* host entries** on PharBP there are
**43 unique genomes** (54 named strains; the rest are unspecified "*Pseudomonas*" and unusable).
*P. putida* KT2440 stands out — many phages (@tbl-hosts).

| host | genome | # PharBP RBPs | # phages |
|---|---|:--:|:--:|
| *P. aeruginosa* PAO1 | GCF_000006765.1 | 3106 | 590 |
| *P. putida* KT2440 | GCF_000007565.2 | 227 | **71** |
| *P. aeruginosa* PA14 | GCF_030264075.1 | 130 | 40 |
| *P. syringae* | GCF_018394375.1 | 192 | 34 |

: PharBP *Pseudomonas* hosts (snippet; 54 named strains / 43 unique genomes). {#tbl-hosts}

## Our receptors × PharBP strains {#sec-presence}

`receptor_host_presence.tsv` combines @tbl-receptor and @tbl-hosts: how **our** receptors are
present across the 54 PharBP strains (# host strains matching at ≥90 / ≥70 / ≥50 % identity, best
host, etc.). This is the key intermediate for indirectly predicting the RBP range for our isolates
(@tbl-presence).

| our_rep | category | hosts ≥90 % id | max identity | best host |
|---|---|:--:|:--:|---|
| BPBBIK_01078 | OmpA | 6 | 97.7 % | *Pseudomonas putida* |
| NEEDOG_04082 | other-OM | 7 | 98.7 % | *Pseudomonas putida* |

# Part B — The folding attempt and why it is a negative result {#sec-fold}

Because both candidate lists were large, we condensed them: for RBPs we kept a representative of
each highly-similar cluster (>90 %); for receptors we kept only plausible phage targets (removed
efflux pumps etc.).

## Condensed candidate lists {#sec-condensed}

`condensed_rbps.tsv` → **114 RBPs**; `condensed_receptors.tsv` → **63 receptors**
(@tbl-rbps, @tbl-recs).

| rbp_id | type | # members | length | host |
|---|:--:|:--:|:--:|---|
| RBP0001 | TF | 25 | 682 | *P. putida* KT2440 |
| RBP0002 | TSP | 20 | 806 | *P. putida* KT2440 / NBRC 14164 |

: Condensed RBPs (snippet; 114 total). {#tbl-rbps}

| rec_id | category | our strains | product |
|---|---|---|---|
| REC014 | FadL | all 5 | Long-chain fatty acid transporter |
| REC006 | Omp-porin | all 5 | OmpW family protein |

: Condensed receptors (snippet; 63 total). {#tbl-recs}

![Blank scaffold before any simulation — 114 RBPs × 63 receptors = **7,182** pairs.](../code/output/0703_phage_host_matrix/fold/rbp_receptor_iptm_heatmap_EMPTY.png){#fig-empty width=80%}

## The simulation {#sec-sim}

`binding_matrix.csv` holds all **7,182** pairs predicted by ESMFold (6,358 folded OK + 824 skipped
for length). `iptm` = interaction/binding score; `ptm` = folding quality; `status` = skipped-or-not
(@tbl-matrix). Large biases follow.

| rbp_id | rec_id | iptm | ptm | status |
|---|---|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| RBP0001 | REC001 | 0.145 | 0.524 | OK |
| RBP0001 | REC002 | 0.137 | 0.534 | OK |

: `binding_matrix.csv` (snippet; 7,182 rows). {#tbl-matrix}

![Final ESMFold pseudo-ipTM matrix. **Left:** rows/cols sorted by length — nearly uniform, with the
brightest cells at smallest-RBP × smallest-receptor (a size artifact, red box). **Right:** the score
correlates with complex length (**r = +0.58**) — it tracks size, not
binding.](../code/output/0703_phage_host_matrix/fold/rbp_receptor_iptm_heatmap.png){#fig-heatmap width=95%}

## Control test for ESMFold {#sec-control}

The matrix gave suspiciously flat scores (everything near 0.13) and the top "hits" tracked protein
size, not any specific pairing. A screen is only meaningful if it can separate a real binder from a
non-binder, so we tested the method against pairs with **known answers**.

**Hypothesis.**

- **H1 (method works):** documented binders should score **above** their scrambled/mismatched
  controls and above the screen background.
- **H0 (null):** the score reflects generic foldability/size, so real ≈ scrambled ≈ background.

**The three positive controls** — experimentally documented pairs, prioritizing solved co-structures
(ground truth) plus one in our own organism; sequences from UniProt/NCBI (@tbl-positives).

| positive pair | RBP accession | receptor accession | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| T5 **pb5** × *E. coli* **FhuA** | P23207 | P06971 | cryo-EM co-structure, PDB **8A8C** |
| λ **gpJ** (C-term RBD) × *E. coli* **LamB** | P03749 | P02943 | co-structure, PDB **8XCJ** |
| DEV **gp54** × *P. aeruginosa* **LptD** | ASZ72261.1 | Q9I5U2 | genetics + AlphaFold, mBio 2026 (our organism) |

: Positive controls and provenance. {#tbl-positives}

For each positive we also folded a **length-matched scrambled** receptor (same residues, shuffled —
removes the size confound) and a **mismatched** receptor, through the identical pipeline
(@fig-control, @tbl-control).

![Control test. **Left:** positives (green) do not exceed scrambled (red) or the screen background
(grey band). **Right:** the clincher — when the receptor is scrambled, whole-complex **pTM collapses**
(the model detects the fake), **but the interface ipTM barely moves** (it is not reading a real
interface).](../code/output/0703_phage_host_matrix/fold/control_validation.png){#fig-control width=95%}

| positive pair | real | scrambled | mismatch | background |
|---|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| T5 pb5 × FhuA (8A8C) | 0.137 | **0.136** | 0.129 | median 0.127 |
| λ gpJ × LamB (8XCJ) | 0.112 | 0.102 | 0.129 | (sd 0.026) |
| DEV gp54 × LptD | 0.159 | 0.129 | 0.112 | |

: Control scores — positives do not separate from negatives or background. {#tbl-control}

::: {.callout-important title="Conclusion — H0 supported, H1 rejected"}
Known binders did not separate from controls (the gold-standard pb5 × FhuA differs from its own
scrambled receptor by **0.001**). Whole-complex **pTM collapses** on scrambling but the interface
**ipTM does not move** → the score is not reading a real interface. **The folding screen is not
informative for RBP–receptor binding, and we do not use it as evidence.** Our receptor-repertoire
overlap (Part A) remains the primary, clue-level readout and does not depend on this step.
:::
